# **1. Defining Mental Health and Mental Illness**

## **1.1 What is Mental Health?**

The terms mental health and mental illness are often used interchangeably, but this is incorrect. Everyone has mental health - whether it is good ("flourishing") or bad ("languishing"), but not everyone lives with a mental illness. In this section, you'll learn how to distinguish between these two distinct terms, and understand how they are inextricably linked.

**Mental health** is defined by the World Health Organization (WHO) as "a state of well-being in which an individual realizes his or her own potential, can cope with the normal stressors of life, can work productively, and can make a contribution to his or her community."

**Mental illness** implies that a person has received a clinical diagnosis and/or is experiencing clinically significant symptoms of mental illness. Mental illnesses envelop a broad categorization of conditions and can be short-lasting episodes or chronic, lifelong disorders.

> Having a mental illness isn't inherently "bad" and having symptoms of a mental illness isn't either. It comes down to what "being healthy" and "recovery" means to each individual.

## **1.2 Who can diagnose mental illnesses?**

In Canada, the following professionals can diagnose mental illness:

-   **Family Physicians**\
    Family physicians are medical doctors primarily trained in family medicine. Family doctors can prescribe medications and may be able to refer or connect you with a provider of psychotherapy.

-   **Psychologists**\
    Psychologists hold a master’s and/or doctoral degree in psychology and often further specialize in specific areas of mental health. Psychologists specialize in providing psychotherapy.

-   **Psychiatrists**\
    Psychiatrists are medical doctors who go on to specialize in mental health and mental disorders. Psychologists can provide pharmacotherapy (prescribe medications) and psychotherapy.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## **1.3 When are mental illnesses diagnosed?**

The timing of developing a mental illness varies based on a number of factors (including biopsychosocial risk factors and the mental illness in question), but research suggests that 75% of mental illnesses occur before the age of 25 ([Kessler et al. 2007](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/17551351/)). 

Given that the average age for post-secondary students ranges from 18-25 - a period also referred to as **emerging adulthood** ([Arnett 2000](http://jeffreyarnett.com/ARNETT_Emerging_Adulthood_theory.pdf)) - students are considered to be a particularly "at risk" group for mental health deterioration. Notably, post-secondary institutions are reporting that more incoming undergraduate students are arriving at school with pre-existing mental illnesses. In fact, recent research suggests that rates of mental illnesses in the post-secondary population are not significantly different from those found among the general Canadian population ([Wiens et al. 2020](https://journals.sagepub.com/doi/full/10.1177/0706743719874178)).

::: callout-note
That's not to say that working towards improving mental health among post-secondary students is unnecessary - quite the opposite. These reports suggest that students are in need of tools and education to help build their resiliency in the face of a myriad of stressors faced over the course of their post-secondary education. We hope that Canada's Student Mental Health Network can provide some of this support to students.
:::

## **1.4 Why is mental health important?**

As you've learned, we all have mental health, and the effects of poor mental health and mental illness can be wide-reaching. The Canadian Mental Health Association (CMHA) reports the following mental health-related statistics(opens in a new tab):

-   Approximately 1 in 5 individuals will experience a mental illness each year.

-   50% of Canadians have experienced, or will experience a mental illness by the age of 40

-   Mental illness will affect all Canadians at some point in their lifetime, either directly or indirectly (through a friend, family member, or acquaintance).

Mental ill health has a significant economic impact, too. The burden of mental illnesses to the Canadian economy was estimated to be \$51 billion in 2003 ([Lim et al., 2008](https://www.canada.ca/content/dam/phac-aspc/migration/phac-aspc/publicat/hpcdp-pspmc/28-3/pdf/cdic28-3-2eng.pdf)), with more recent projections estimating the total cumulative costs over the next 30 years will exceed \$2.5 trillion ([Smetanin et al., 2011](https://www.mentalhealthcommission.ca/wp-content/uploads/drupal/MHCC_Report_Base_Case_FINAL_ENG_0_0.pdf)). This reflects both direct costs (i.e., healthcare) and indirect costs (i.e., loss of employee productivity, short- and long-term disability claims). In 2012, CMHA [reported](https://www.mentalhealthcommission.ca/wp-content/uploads/drupal/2016-06/Investing_in_Mental_Health_FINAL_Version_ENG.pdf) that approximately one fifth (21.4%) of the working Canadian population experienced either poor mental health or a mental illness, negatively impacting their productivity.

# **2. The Dual Continuum of Mental Health and Illness**


## **2.1 Connecting Mental Health and Mental Illness**

While mental health and mental illness are distinct concepts, they are inextricably connected. In his groundbreaking 2002 [paper](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/12096700/), Corey Keyes established the Dual Continuum of Mental Health and Mental Illness. Since its publication, the Dual Continuum has been widely adopted by subject matter experts and practitioners around the world studying mental health or providing mental health care.

This model conceptualizes mental health and mental illness as separate, but interconnected continuums. Mental health can range from good (or "flourishing") to poor (or "languishing"), sitting anywhere along that spectrum. Our mental health moves flexibly along this continuum from day to day, month to month, etc. Similarly, an individual can move along the mental illness continuum, ranging from no mental illness to severe mental illness. Importantly, the severity of a mental illness can be influenced by frequency, longevity, and severity of individual symptoms, in addition to the degree to which the illness is being managed.

Importantly, it is possible for an individual to experience good mental health (or to "flourish") while living with a well-managed mental illness. Similarly, it is possible for an individual to experience poor mental health without meeting the clinical threshold for a mental illness. In the best-case scenario, we would find ourselves in the upper right-hand quadrant of the Dual Continuum model, with good mental health and no mental illness. In the worst case scenario, someone "in crisis" might  find themselves in the bottom left-hand quadrant of the model, with poor mental health and severe mental illness.

::: callout-note
Remember: It isn't inherently "bad" to live with a mental illness. Many people live with well-managed, lifelong mental illnesses (such as chronic anxiety, or even more complex mental illnesses like bipolar disorder) and still experience "flourishing" mental health.
:::

# **3. Risk Factors for Mental Illness**

## **3.1 What Affects your Mental Health?**

Mental health is complex, and can be affected by social, psychological, and biological factors. Certain aspects can place individuals at increased risk for experiencing deterioration in their mental health and/or the development of a mental illness. Fluctuations in our mental health are common and normal, and almost never stem from a sole reason.

    <button id="tbtn-1" onclick="switchTab(1)" style="flex:1; padding: 1.6em 1em; font-size: 0.75rem; font-weight: 700; letter-spacing: 0.1em; text-transform: uppercase; text-align: center; cursor: pointer; background: #f0f2f5; color: #999; border: none; border-right: 1px solid #dde3ec; border-bottom: 3px solid transparent;">Biological</button>
    <button id="tbtn-2" onclick="switchTab(2)" style="flex:1; padding: 1.6em 1em; font-size: 0.75rem; font-weight: 700; letter-spacing: 0.1em; text-transform: uppercase; text-align: center; cursor: pointer; background: #f0f2f5; color: #999; border: none; border-bottom: 3px solid transparent;">Psychological</button>
  </div>

  <div id="tab-0" style="display:block; padding: 2em 2.2em; background: white;">
    <p style="font-size: 0.88rem; line-height: 1.7; color: #333; margin: 0 0 1em 0;"><strong style="color:#1C2944;">Social risk factors</strong> for the development of mental illness or mental health deterioration can include:</p>
    <ul style="font-size: 0.88rem; line-height: 1.7; color: #333; padding-left: 1.4em; margin: 0;">
      <li style="margin-bottom:0.5em;">Lack of social support and/or isolation from others</li>
      <li style="margin-bottom:0.5em;">Abusive relationships</li>
      <li style="margin-bottom:0.5em;">Weak social safety net (family and community factors)</li>
      <li style="margin-bottom:0.5em;">Low socioeconomic status</li>
      <li>Exposure to discrimination</li>
    </ul>
  </div>

  <div id="tab-1" style="display:none; padding: 2em 2.2em; background: white;">
    <p style="font-size: 0.88rem; line-height: 1.7; color: #333; margin: 0 0 1em 0;"><strong style="color:#1C2944;">Biological risk factors</strong> for the development of mental illness or mental health deterioration can include:</p>
    <ul style="font-size: 0.88rem; line-height: 1.7; color: #333; padding-left: 1.4em; margin: 0;">
      <li style="margin-bottom:0.5em;">Genetic vulnerability</li>
      <li style="margin-bottom:0.5em;">Health comorbidities (or generally poor physical health)</li>
      <li style="margin-bottom:0.5em;">Poor nutrition or sleep patterns</li>
      <li style="margin-bottom:0.5em;">Neurological deficits or injuries</li>
      <li>Substance abuse</li>
    </ul>
  </div>

  <div id="tab-2" style="display:none; padding: 2em 2.2em; background: white;">
    <p style="font-size: 0.88rem; line-height: 1.7; color: #333; margin: 0 0 1em 0;"><strong style="color:#1C2944;">Psychological risk factors</strong> for the development of mental illness or mental health deterioration can include:</p>
    <ul style="font-size: 0.88rem; line-height: 1.7; color: #333; padding-left: 1.4em; margin: 0;">
      <li style="margin-bottom:0.5em;">Prolonged exposure to stress</li>
      <li style="margin-bottom:0.5em;">Traumatic experience(s)</li>
      <li style="margin-bottom:0.5em;">Dissatisfaction with current life status</li>
      <li style="margin-bottom:0.5em;">Self-depreciation</li>
      <li>Certain personality traits, thoughts, emotions, and attitudes</li>
    </ul>
  </div>

</div>

<script>
function switchTab(idx) {
  for (let i = 0; i < 3; i++) {
    const btn = document.getElementById('tbtn-' + i);
    const panel = document.getElementById('tab-' + i);
    if (i === idx) {
      btn.style.background = 'white';
      btn.style.color = '#1C2944';
      btn.style.borderBottom = '3px solid #1C2944';
      panel.style.display = 'block';
    } else {
      btn.style.background = '#f0f2f5';
      btn.style.color = '#999';
      btn.style.borderBottom = '3px solid transparent';
      panel.style.display = 'none';
    }
  }
}
</script>

## **3.2 The Link Between Physical and Mental Health**

Physical and mental health are interdependent on one another. There are a multitude of physical factors that can influence your mental health, but we will focus below on the following three: diet, physical activity, and sleep.

```{=html}
<style>
  .pmh-item { display: flex; align-items: flex-start; gap: 1em; margin-bottom: 0.5em; font-family: 'Open Sans', sans-serif; }
  .pmh-circle { flex-shrink: 0; width: 180px; height: 180px; border-radius: 50%; overflow: hidden; }
  .pmh-circle img { width: 100%; height: 100%; object-fit: cover; display: block; }
  .pmh-circle.placeholder { display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; font-size: 3rem; }
  .pmh-content { flex: 1; }
  .pmh-title { font-size: 1rem; font-weight: 700; color: #1C2944; margin: 0 0 0.5em 0; }
  .pmh-body { font-size: 0.88rem; line-height: 1.75; color: #333; margin: 0 0 0.6em 0; }
  .pmh-body a { color: #1C2944; font-weight: 600; }
  .pmh-divider { border: none; border-top: 1px solid #dde3ec; margin: 0 0 2.5em 0; }
</style>

<div style="margin: 0; padding: 0.5rem 0;">
  <div class="pmh-item">
    <div class="pmh-circle"><img src="images/module1-img9.jpg" alt="Diet"/></div>
    <div class="pmh-content">
      <p class="pmh-title">Diet</p>
      <p class="pmh-body">What we decide to eat and drink can have a significant influence on the development, management, and prevention of mental illness and mental health deterioration. Evidence suggests that nutrition is a protective factor against depression and anxiety, while an unhealthy diet acts as a risk factor (<a href="#">Lim et al. 2016</a>).</p>
      <p class="pmh-body">A healthy diet is defined by sufficient macro (carbohydrates, fats, and protein) and micronutrient (vitamins and minerals) consumption. See <a href="https://food-guide.canada.ca/en/" target="_blank">Canada's Food Guide</a> for more detail on achieving and maintaining a healthy diet.</p>
    </div>
  </div>
  <hr class="pmh-divider">

  <div class="pmh-item">
    <div class="pmh-circle"><img src="images/module1-img10.jpg" alt="Physical Activity"/></div>
    <div class="pmh-content">
      <p class="pmh-title">Physical Activity</p>
      <p class="pmh-body">Staying physically active not only keeps you physically healthy, but mentally healthy too (<a href="#" target="_blank">Tyson et al. 2010</a>). Evidence suggests that endorphins released during exercise result in positive mental health effects. As little as 10 minutes of physical exercise can have a positive effect on energy, mood, and mental alertness, though adults should aim to get 150 mins of moderate-to-vigorous physical activity per week. Check out <a href="https://www.canada.ca/en/public-health/services/being-active/physical-activity-guidelines-canadians.html" target="_blank">Canada's Physical Activity Guidelines</a> for more information.</p>
      <p class="pmh-body">No time to get to the gym? Remember that exercise can also be: walking, doing household chores, raking leaves or shovelling snow, etc. There are also online resources that can help you exercise outside of the gym (<a href="https://www.nike.com/ntc-app" target="_blank">Nike Training Club App</a>, <a href="https://www.youtube.com/user/yogawithadriene" target="_blank">Yoga with Adriene</a>).</p>
    </div>
  </div>
  <hr class="pmh-divider">

  <div class="pmh-item">
    <div class="pmh-circle"><img src="images/module1-img11.jpg" alt="Sleep"/></div>
    <div class="pmh-content">
      <p class="pmh-title">Sleep</p>
      <p class="pmh-body">We get that achieving the recommended 7–9 hours of sleep every night isn't always possible. However, it's important to note that lack of sleep increases the risk of mental health deterioration and the development of some mental illnesses. Lack of sleep can also cause heightened stress and irritability, while good quality sleep has been found to improve mental health and overall well-being (<a href="#" target="_blank">Scott et al. 2021</a>).</p>
      <p class="pmh-body">On the flip side, mood and mental health can drastically affect sleep quality. Individuals with anxiety or heightened levels of stress tend to have more issues with sleep, making this a bit of a double edged sword. Resources for improving your sleep are provided by the <a href="https://www.mayoclinic.org/healthy-lifestyle/adult-health/in-depth/sleep/art-20048379" target="_blank">Mayo Clinic</a> and <a href="https://anxietycanada.com/articles/sleep-and-anxiety/" target="_blank">CMHA BC/Anxiety Canada</a>.</p>
    </div>
  </div>

</div>
```

```{=html}
<div class="section-summary">
  <h3>3.3 Section Summary</h3>
  <ul>
    <li>Social, biological, and psychological factors can increase our risk of developing a mental illness or experiencing mental health deterioration.</li>
    <li>Some of these factors may be out of our control (i.e., genetic vulnerabilities), while others are very much within our control (i.e., nutrition, physical activity, and sleep quality).</li>
    <li>Our physical and mental health are closely related - taking care of ourselves physically can help us to maintain good mental health.</li>
  </ul>
</div>
```
